# beowulf-fitt-35 — cruces worth recording in QUESTIONS.md (pass 2)

Each: line · word · what was chosen · why disputed.

- 2468 · `tō sār` · "too sorely" (Klaeber’s italic t). The apparatus gives MS `sio`; editors read `swā` (Rieger, Grein, Ettmüller, Holthausen 1-2, Sedgefield), `giō` (Holthausen 3) or drop it (Schücking). Half-line called shaky.
- 2473 · `wīd` · "wide". MS `rid` (transcript A); `wīd` is Grundtvig’s translation’s repair. The water is not named.
- 2475–77 · `oððe him Ongenðeowes eaferan wǣran … ofer heafo` · `oððe` kept "or" (i "or rather"); `heafo` "seas" (Sarrazin `heaþo` "battle"); `Hrēosnabeorh` (Bugge, Sedgefield `Hrefna beorh`).
- 2481 · `ōðer his ealdre gebohte` · no object; Grein inserts [hit] and keeps his, Heyne/Schücking/Sedgefield read `hit` for `his`, Holder/Holthausen/Chambers read as Klaeber.
- 2482 · `onsǣge` · "fatal" (adjective or noun; sense a guess).
- 2484–86 · `mǣg ōðerne … on bonan stǣlan`, `Eofores nīosað` · "avenged the other on the slayer"; who is who is inferred from the following lines; `nīosað` kept as historic present (Grein `nīosade`).
- 2488 · `[hilde]blāc` · Klaeber’s supply, the MS has only `blāc`; `[heoro-]` (Grein et al.), `[hrēa-]` (Bugge), `[hilde-]` (Holthausen + 4 editors, metri causa).
- 2492 · `ēðelwyn` · "homeland-joy" (Sievers `-wynne`).
- 2500–02 · `þæt mec ǣr ond sīð oft gelǣste` · full stop after `gelǣste` in Grein, Schücking, Sedgefield; and `Dæghrefne … tō handbonan, Hūga cempan`: Dæghrefn’s link with the Frisian raid (2354–2359) is inference.
- 2503–05 · `Frēscyning[e]`, `campe` · -e from Grundtvig’s translation; MS `cempan`, Kemble and four editors `campe` "in the fight" (italic a, e).
- 2514 · `mǣrðu` · accusative plural "deeds of glory" (MS `mærðū` = `mǣrðum`; Kemble `mǣrðo`; Chambers keeps -um).
- 2509 · `heard sweord` / `heardsweord` (Morgan, Holthausen, Sedgefield).
- 2518–21 · `gylpe wiðgrīpan` · "grapple … in boast", i "make good my vow" (Schröer `gūþe` "in war"); `āglǣcean` root unsettled.
- 2523 · `[o]reðes ond attres` · MS `reðes ⁊ hattres`; `[o]` Grein, `attres` Grundtvig/Kemble; italic a.
- 2525 · `[furður]` · Klaeber’s supply (Chambers); alternatives `[fǣhðo]` (Schubert, Barnouw, Trautmann), `[feohte]` (Bugge, Schücking), `furðor` (Archiv). Also `oferfleôn` (MS ofer fleon; Bugge, Barnouw, Sedgefield flēo(ha)n; Trautmann forflēon).
- 2527–28 · `gylp ofersitte` · "forgo boast"; Sievers `þæs` for `þæt`.
- 2533–34 · `nefn(e)`, `þæt` (italic þæ; MS `wat`) · restored/altered letters.
- 2540–41 · `strengo getrūwọde`, `earges sīð` · case of `strengo` open; `earges` taken as noun.
- 2545–49 · `sto[n]dan` (Thorpe); `dēop gedȳgan` · noun "the deep" (Grundtvig `dēor` "animal", Bugge/Sedgefield `dēor` "bold").
- 2552–56 · `hlynnan`, `friclan`, `From ǣrest cwōm` · rare/unique verbs, "forth" adverb vs adjective.
- 2559 · `onswāf` and `Biorn` · "swung" (a guess); Sedgefield `born`.
- 2561 · `hringbogan` · the dragon (Sarrazin `hringboran` = Beowulf); one letter.
- 2564 · `anglāw` · MS `unglaw` (erasure), Thorpe `unslēaw`, Bugge + 4 editors `unslāw`; "not dull" a guess; Klaeber’s form not in the lexica.
- 2567 · `winia` · Grundtvig’s translation `wigena`.
- 2570 · `tō gescipe` · "to its fate"; Thorpe `gesceape`, Ettmüller `gescepe`, Heyne `gescīfe` "headlong" (with `tō` in 2569b), Holthausen/Sedgefield likewise.
- 2570–72 · `þonne his myne sōhte` · "than his desire sought"; whose mind/desire is open (cf. 2572 `myne`, QUESTIONS note on 1797).
- 2573–75 · `ðǣr hē þȳ fyrste forman dōgọre wealdan mōste, swā him wyrd ne gescrāf hrēð æt hilde` · construction disputed (`swā` "as/though", `mōste` mood); best reading given.
- 2575–77 · `incge-lāfe` · Kemble `īcge-`, Thorpe/Ettmüller/Sedgefield `Incges`, Grundtvig `Ingwina` (?), Holthausen `Ingwines`, Trautmann `isigre`/`irfe-`, Holthausen `yrringca`/`æðelincges`; "heirloom of Incg" a guess.
- 2589 · `[ofer] willan` · Rieger + 4 editors; Grein `[wyrmes]`, Aant. `[wyrme tō]` ("at the worm’s will").
- 2593–94 · `nīwan stefne` · "with a new turn", as 1787.
- 2599–2601 · `sefa wið sorgum`, `sibb’ … wiht onwendan` · `wið` "against/amid"; the maxim read with `wiht` as subject.
